hypotheses.title: Net Income Forecast Dispersion Compression and Institutional Consensus Clarity
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Analyst earnings forecast dispersion (adj_net_income_stddev) measures institutional disagreement and future operational uncertainty. According to the Diether-Malloy-Scherbina disagreement anomaly, equities with high analyst dispersion suffer from speculative retail overbidding and severe future underperformance. Normalizing dispersion via ts_rank over a 252-day trailing baseline (-ts_rank(ts_backfill(adj_net_income_stddev, 60), 252)) isolates equities entering periods of high institutional earnings clarity and low surprise risk. Paired with liquidity dampening to prevent micro-cap churn.
confounders: Uncontested consensus clarity that accurately anticipates terminal corporate revenue contraction
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if low dispersion equities suffer higher earnings announcement volatility than high dispersion peers.

hypotheses.title: Annual EPS Estimate Standard Deviation Compression Anomaly
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Measures consensus dispersion across annual diluted earnings per share forecasts (anl4_afv4_dts_spe). When Wall Street analysts converge on tight EPS estimates relative to the firm's 1-year historical range, valuation ambiguity drops and institutional fundamental allocators expand long positions. Z-score normalization within subindustries neutralizes sector-wide cyclical differences.
confounders: Low analyst coverage where low standard deviation reflects lack of research interest rather than fundamental certainty
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if firms with compressed EPS forecast variance deliver lower forward returns than the broad market.

hypotheses.title: Analyst Consensus Clarity and Intraday VWAP Mean-Reversion Synergy
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Combines structural analyst consensus clarity (70% weight on compressed net income forecast dispersion) with 5-day intraday VWAP mean-reversion (30% weight). The fundamental dispersion component provides low-turnover medium-term direction, while the VWAP reversion component captures short-term microstructure liquidity provision, optimizing overall information coefficient and turnover balance.
confounders: Strong momentum regimes where intraday VWAP deviations persist without mean reverting
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if combining VWAP reversion increases portfolio turnover without improving Sharpe ratio.
